writeup.headline: Philadelphia Eagles to win (-198)
writeup.analysis: Philadelphia Eagles sit at 2-0 overall and remain undefeated on the road at 1-0, which matters given they are traveling to Chicago for this contest. Their recent trajectory is strong, with wins in their last two games following three consecutive losses, suggesting they have corrected course and are building momentum at the right time. The Chicago Bears, by contrast, sit at 1-1 and have struggled at home with an 0-1 record in their own building, an immediate red flag for a team trying to protect its house. The Bears' own recent form is more volatile, posting a 1-2 record over their last five games compared to the Philadelphia Eagles' 2-0 finish to that same span. On the injury front, the Chicago Bears are substantially depleted, with five players listed as unavailable, including Anthony Johnson Jr., Caleb Williams, Shemar Turner, Noah Sewell, and Kyler Gordon. The Philadelphia Eagles do carry injuries of their own (Fred Johnson out, Dallas Goedert out, Jonathan Greenard questionable, Hollywood Brown out, Landon Dickerson in injured reserve), but the depth and scope of Chicago's losses, particularly at quarterback with Caleb Williams out, creates a structural disadvantage that should favor Philadelphia's opportunity to impose its will. Given that the Bears have already shown vulnerability at home and the Philadelphia Eagles have demonstrated resilience and consistency on the road, expect Philadelphia to control the tempo and execution in this matchup. The combination of Philadelphia Eagles' proven road poise, Chicago Bears' home struggles, and the Bears' critical personnel absences creates a clear edge for the visiting side.
